title: Planets for Kids! 5 Space Surprises with Nova
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Nova, your robot space buddy, and welcome to Space Kids Academy!
Today we're blasting off to visit five amazing planets. Every planet has a super surprise.
Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
Ready? Three, two, one, blast off!

lines: Here's our first planet. Here's a clue: it's the smallest planet, and the closest to the Sun! Can you guess?
Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system.
It's covered in craters, like little dents made by space rocks.
Can you curl up small, like tiny Mercury?
Can you guess how long one year is on Mercury?
Only 88 days! Mercury zooms around the Sun super fast.
Mercury is the fastest planet in our solar system.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's the hottest planet, and it shines bright in the night sky! Can you guess?
Venus is covered in thick, yellow clouds.
Venus is the hottest planet, even hotter than Mercury!
Can you fan yourself like it's super hot? Phew!
Can you guess which way Venus spins?
Backward! On Venus, the Sun comes up in the west.
Venus is the brightest planet we can see in the night sky.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's red, and robots are driving on it! Can you guess?
Mars is called the Red Planet.
Mars has ice caps at the top and the bottom, a little like Earth.
Can you drive like a little robot rover? Beep, beep!
Can you guess why Mars is red?
Rust! The dirt on Mars has iron in it, and it turned rusty red.
Robot rovers are exploring Mars right now, taking pictures for us.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's the biggest planet of all! Can you guess?
Jupiter is so big, more than one thousand Earths could fit inside!
Jupiter has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.
Can you spin around slowly, like a big storm? Spin, spin!
Can you guess? Can you stand on Jupiter?
No! Jupiter is made mostly of gas, so there's no ground to stand on.
Jupiter has lots of moons. More than ninety!
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has big, beautiful rings! Can you guess?
Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock, from tiny bits to pieces as big as a house.
Saturn is the second biggest planet.
Can you draw a big ring in the air with your finger? Round and round!
Can you guess? What would happen if you put Saturn in a giant bathtub?
It would float! Saturn is very light for its size.
Saturn has more moons than any other planet!

recap: What a space adventure! Let's remember.
A year on Mercury is only 88 days.
Mars is red because of rust.
And Saturn could float in a giant bathtub!
outro: Which planet was your favorite? Keep looking up at the stars, and keep learning.
Bye, friends! See you in space!
